correctness.rationale: In each standard Plücker chart the quadric is det(I+BB^T) by Cauchy–Binet; its gradient is 2 adj(I+BB^T)B. At corank one, a nonzero kernel vector v cannot satisfy B^T v=0 since (I+BB^T)v would then equal v. Thus exactly the corank-at-least-two points are singular. For radical R of dimension r, the derivative of the isotropy equations at R surjects onto Sym²(R*) because V/R→R* via q is surjective and the field has characteristic zero. This yields dim OGr(r,n)=r(n−r)−r(r+1)/2, also at maximal isotropy. The nondegenerate (k−r)-plane in R^⊥/R gives a nonempty open Grassmannian fiber of dimension (k−r)(n−k−r). Adding, and taking the maximum over exact radical strata, gives both dimension claims for every admissible r, including r=2. The recorded symbolic checks are finite consistency checks, not the proof.
residual_risks: The conclusion is about the underlying loci over C, and does not assert that every threefold in the Grassmannian meets the singular locus or that these dimension arguments determine scheme multiplicities.

evidence: Bagno–Cherniavsky give B-congruence orbit closures by simultaneous upper-left rectangular rank bounds, with codimension (inv+exc)/2 for a full symmetric permutation matrix. This is an exact theorem for all symmetric n×n matrices, not merely an expected-codimension formula. Wyser gives the related flag-orbit description by restrictions of an orthogonal form. Denham–Schulze–Walther concern configuration hypersurfaces, a different application.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The full-rank form space is an open subset, and its rank condition at the k×k corner pulls back along the smooth Gram map from GL_n to exactly the preimage of the radical condition under the smooth projection to Gr(k,n). Thus the broader dimension theorem applies without a genericity assumption about arbitrary sections.

evidence: For given (k,r), take the involution swapping the adjacent length-r blocks [k−r+1,k] and [k+1,k+r] in order, and fixing other indices. Its upper-left i×j rank is min(i,j,k−r+(i−k)_++(j−k)_+). A symmetric matrix with k×k corner of rank ≤k−r satisfies every one of these bounds, by deleting rows and columns beyond k; conversely take i=j=k. Lemma 5.2 therefore gives exactly this corner-rank locus as the orbit closure. The involution has r² inversions and r excedances, so Theorems 7.4 and 8.1 give codimension r(r+1)/2.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The closure meets invertible forms at its permutation matrix, and exact corner rank k−r is a nonempty open condition there. For g∈GL_n, the rank of the corner of g^Tg equals the rank of q on the plane spanned by the first k columns. The Gram map to invertible symmetric forms and the projection to the Grassmannian are smooth surjective (fibers respectively orthogonal translates and parabolic translates), preserving codimension on pullback. This proves the same all-r count from the earlier dimension theorem; putting r=2 together with the earlier singular ideal gives the headline claim.

evidence: Friedman–Hoşten–Rosana Proposition 2.4 gives the all-k singular ideal in terms of the cocircuit Gram entries H_ij, beyond the numerical bound in their Theorem 2.3. For a row chart [I_k B], the first k cocircuit vectors are, up to signs, the wedges of all but one of the chart rows. Their pairings are exactly the signed complementary minors of the row Gram matrix. The remaining cocircuit vectors lie in the span of those k vectors.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Vanishing of all H_ij is equivalent on each chart to vanishing of the adjugate of the restriction form. Thus the earlier ideal identifies exactly the radical-at-least-two underlying set for all k. The earlier lines case also already supplies codimension three for k=2.

originality.rationale: The all-k singular-set description is equivalent to the earlier all-k singular ideal in Friedman–Hoşten–Rosana. The all-r dimension formula is a specialization of earlier exact rank-control orbit dimensions for symmetric matrices, not just of a generic expected-codimension statement. Both parts are covered without relying on a later catalogue duplicate or on inaccessible literature.
residual_risks: The exact Agrachev–Gamkrelidze citation was not independently verified. No claim is made about the earliest specialized wording; earlier mathematical implication is sufficient for the decision.

value.rationale: The exact codimension is relevant in the Euclidean-distance application and the short chart proof is useful exposition. But the singular set translates an existing ideal, and the dimension assertion is a directly computable case of a stronger rank-control theorem. The record gives no distinct new geometric or optimization consequence after crediting these prior results; its own scope explicitly excludes a stronger ED-generality obstruction.
residual_risks: No downstream statement about degrees, multiplicities, or intersections with specified models has been evaluated as a surviving claim.
